subject: Proposal: Availability exception framework and monthly credit mechanics
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeindustries.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Cc: contracts@acmeindustries.com
Date: 2026-11-18T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Request: temporary SLA exception for scheduled maintenance windows

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the performance looks promising for our search and summarization workloads. Before we move to procurement, our operations team asked whether Redwood can accept a limited SLA exception tied to pre-planned maintenance windows.

Specifically: can we agree to a standard 99.95% monthly uptime for production, but allow up to 3 scheduled maintenance windows per quarter (each up to 6 hours) that are excluded from uptime calculations? In return, Acme would accept a smaller monthly credit for availability lapses during those scheduled windows (we can share a maintenance calendar).

Two asks from our side:
- A short example of how credits would be calculated if an outage overlaps a scheduled window.
- A brief template we can share with our procurement team to show the carve-out language.

I copied contracts so they have context. Expecting to move quickly — do you have a draft we can look at by Monday?

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Director, Platform Ops
Acme Industries

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acmeindustries.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, contracts@acmeindustries.com
Date: 2026-11-18T18:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exception for scheduled maintenance windows

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. We can work with a scheduled-maintenance carve-out; below is a pragmatic approach that balances predictability for Acme and operational flexibility for Redwood. I attached a short template and a sample calendar (you'll see the CSV).

Proposal (high level):
- Base production availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Scheduled maintenance carve-out: up to 3 scheduled maintenance windows per rolling quarter, each up to 6 hours, provided Redwood gives >= 72 hours advance notice.
- Overlap rule: any incident time that falls entirely within a pre-notified scheduled window is excluded from uptime calculations. If an incident starts outside and continues into a scheduled window, only the portion outside the scheduled window is counted toward downtime.
- Credit mechanics: monthly service credits remain capped at 30% of that month's invoice. Credits are applied pro rata on the affected model route(s). During scheduled windows, we propose a reduced credit rate of 25% of what the equivalent non-scheduled outage credit would be for the overlapping duration. Example: a 3-hour outage during standard time that would normally trigger $6,000 in credits would be treated as $1,500 when fully inside a scheduled window under the reduced-rate assumption.

I'll escalate to Ben and Marissa on the commercial/legal side for redlines on cap and notice periods. If that framework looks reasonable, we can deliver a clean redline Monday morning.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>, Elena Park <elena.park@acmeindustries.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, contracts@acmeindustries.com
Date: 2026-11-19T09:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exception for scheduled maintenance windows

Looping in the commercial perspective. Two quick points:

1) Credit math: the example Laura gave is fine directionally, but we should convert to a clean formula for procurement. Suggest: monthly_credit = min( invoice_monthly * outage_minutes / total_month_minutes * standard_credit_rate, invoice_monthly * credit_cap ). For scheduled windows the "standard_credit_rate" becomes 0.25 * standard_credit_rate.

2) Pricing/term trade: since Acme is asking for the carve-out, we should request a 6- or 12-month committed volume (reserved capacity) or a modest uplift (~6%) on published Dedicated pricing. That trade makes the exception commercially neutral for us. Happy to mark that as optional in the term sheet.

I attached a draft term line and asked Marissa to route a redline back to Acme's contracts.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exception for scheduled maintenance windows

Elena / team —

Attached is a redline that adds the scheduled-maintenance carve-out into the SLA template and clarifies notice requirements, outage overlap treatment, and adjusted credit rate during scheduled windows. Key legal points we retained:
- Scheduled windows require >=72 hours notice and must be in a published calendar (we received Acme's sample CSV; thanks).
- Incident overlap described as Laura proposed (only out-of-window minutes count).
- Monthly credit cap remains at 30% of the invoice; scheduled-window credit uses the reduced rate and is counted within the cap.
- Exceptions for emergency maintenance (no notice) are excluded from the carve-out and treated per standard SLA rules.

Please review the PDF redline ("acme-sla-exception-redline.pdf"). If Acme confirms the calendar cadence and committed term option (Ben's note), we can prepare an execution-ready addendum.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
